podcast.title: 1950s Decline and Late 1960s Revival
podcast.body: The genre experienced a decline in popularity in the 1950s with the rise of rock music but underwent a significant revival in the late 1960s. "Bluegrass kind of faded away a bit in the 1950s when rock became popular but then it had a revival in the late 60s."

podcast.title: CBGB's Original Music Policy
podcast.body: When Hilly Crystal bought the club that would become CBGB, he initially named it to reflect his music policy, which included country, bluegrass, and blues, among "other music for uplifting gourmandizers." "He named it after his music policy, the kinds of acts he would book, country, blue grass and blues and other music for uplifting gourmandizers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: CBGB's Original Policy
podcast.body: CBGB, founded in 1973, was initially designated as "CBGB and OMFUG" to reflect its original musical policy, which encompassed Bluegrass, along with Country and Blues, and "Other Music for Uplifting Gormandizers." This initial programming direction soon changed as the club became a seminal venue for punk rock. "He called it CBGB an Umfug, which spells out its musical policy. Country, bluegrass, blues, and other music for uplifting Gorman Dysers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Foundations and Characteristics
podcast.body: Bluegrass has its roots in mountain music and is a mixture of gospel, blues, and country. It is distinctly known for its use of the banjo and fiddle, as well as the beautiful close harmonies typically sung in trios or quartets. The fiddle music of Appalachia and the Ozarks forms part of its very foundation. "Bluegrass has its roots in mountain music. Like rock it's really a mixture of many other genres too."

podcast.title: New Influence in Alt Rock (Late 2000s)
podcast.body: Bluegrass was considered as a potential new musical influence for the alt-rock crowd in the late 2000s, alongside folk. This experimentation emerged as rock entered a phase of innovation during its cyclical decline. "Could the industry maybe sell a form of folk and bluegrass influence music to the alt-rock crowd?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Roots Music Category
podcast.body: Bluegrass is recognized as a type of roots music that needs space for expression and appreciation, alongside other traditional forms like hillbilly music. "However, there does need to be space made for all types of roots music, including blue grass and hillbilly music."
